source_caption:
One of the most charming stop-motion movies ever made was built one tiny movement at a time. 🦊

For Fantastic Mr. Fox, Wes Anderson and his team didn’t rely on computers to bring the characters to life. The puppets were physically moved, photographed, moved again, and photographed again — creating the illusion of movement frame by frame.

Anderson wanted the movie to feel handmade, so the sets were packed with tiny details, from miniature houses and farms to real-looking food and costumes. The foxes were made with real fur, and the animators even gave the characters slightly imperfect movements instead of making everything look too smooth.

The production took years, with animators sometimes spending an entire day creating only a few seconds of footage.

It’s that handmade quality that makes Fantastic Mr. Fox feel so different. You can almost see the fingerprints behind every frame.

source_details.title: Fantastic Mr. Fox
source_details.synopsis: Fantastic Mr. Fox is a 2009 adventure comedy film directed by Wes Anderson, who co-wrote it with Noah Baumbach, based on the 1970 novel by Roald Dahl. It stars George Clooney, Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Willem Dafoe, and Owen Wilson. In the stop-motion animated film, a spree of thefts led by Mr. Fox (Clooney) results in his family, and later his community, being hunted down by three farmers. Development on the project began in 2004 as a collaboration between Anderson and Henry Selick under Revolution Studios; by 2007, Revolution and Selick left for other projects. Work on Fantastic Mr. Fox was moved to 20th Century Fox, where production began in 2007 on Stage C of 3 Mills
